last_analysis: Scores are hidden, so the only evidence is that every trial trained without errors and stayed well inside the caps. Prior expectations still matter. Training designs are random and endless, so fresh data should help generalisation, which favours fewer epochs and more samples. The exact-build bonus comes at the end of the episode, which favours gamma 0.98 and lambda 0.95. The cheapest wins come from recipe changes on the cheap baseline network, because a bigger network costs samples. This is the last round, and all trials compete for selection. So I combine the changes most likely to help into three different candidates. (1) r3c1 with twice as many gradient steps per update, because 1 epoch with 16 minibatches gives only about 1,600 gradient steps in total. (2) The deeper context network on the r3c1 recipe. (3) The baseline at 2 epochs with the long-horizon settings, as a middle point between sample reuse and fresh data.
